claims.source_quote_ar: من أعظم الآيات أن يواجه بهذا الكلام رجل واحد أمّة
claims.claim_ar: الأمر الإنشائي «قُلْ فَأْتُوا...» يعمل كتحدٍ مباشر ليثبت البينات
claims.claim_en: The imperative (قُلْ فَأْتُوا...) functions as a performative command — a direct challenge to produce equivalent surahs.
claims.needs_review_reason: The commentary quote emphasizes the confrontational force of the verse, but it does not explicitly label it 'انشائي'; the classification as an 'injāʾ/imperative performative' is inferred from the imperative verb in the ayah.

claims.source_quote_ar: ما من رسول إلا واجه قومه بهذا القول
claims.claim_ar: تكرار نفس التحدّي والمواجهة عبر رسل الله: توظيف أسلوب متكرر لتأكيد الحجة
claims.claim_en: Repetition: the same challenge recurs with every messenger — the invocation is a repeated rhetorical device used by the prophets.

claims.source_quote_ar: شبه فريق الكافرين بالأعمى والأصم، وفريق المؤمنين بالبصير والسميع
claims.claim_ar: تشبيه: تصوير الكافرين كأعمى وأصم والمؤمنين كبصير وسميع لإظهار التباين بين الفريقين
claims.claim_en: Simile: likening the disbelievers to the blind/deaf and the believers to the seeing/hearing, thereby heightening contrast between the groups.
claims.needs_review_reason: The commentary passage explicitly describes this simile, but it appears to comment on a cluster of verses; check scope to ensure it is intended for this specific ayah (11:13) rather than an adjacent verse.

claims.claim_ar: طباق/مقابلة لغوية بين صفات متقابلة (مثلاً: أعمى/بصير، أصم/سميع) لتكثيف الدلالة
claims.claim_en: Antithesis (tibāq): pairing opposite attributes (e.g., blind/seeing, deaf/hearing) to intensify the semantic contrast.
claims.needs_review_reason: The commentary explicitly names 'اللف والطباق', so identification is confident; verify the exact locus (which verse(s) the commentary targets).

claims.source_quote_ar: إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَرُونَ تفترون على الله الكذب باتخاذكم الأوثان له شركاء.
claims.claim_ar: استعمال وصفية اتهامية («مُفْتَرُونَ») لتكعيب الخصم ولتجريمه بلاغياً؛ بلاغة التعييب والتمثيل
claims.claim_en: Use of the accusatory predicate 'مufterūn' (they fabricate) to rhetorically stigmatize the addressees — a condemnatory epithet attributing falsehood.
claims.needs_review_reason: Labeling this usage as 'kināyah' (an indirect/euphemistic or metonymic epithet) is interpretive; the commentary gives the accusatory sense but does not formalize the rhetorical category.

warnings: Provided source chunks are from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) — the developer instruction listed other classical rhetoricians (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, tafsir balāgha). Claims below are drawn only from the supplied chunks; additional authors were not available.

Some quoted commentary passages appear to treat a cluster of verses or nearby verses; confirm whether each rhetorical observation in the commentary is intended specifically for S11:A13 or for adjacent vv.
